text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Civil service strike on October 17, not expected to reach proportions of 1995 winter strikes.
-- Futures market Matif SA will not carry out a co-operation project with German equivalent DTB.
-- Finnish mark re-enters the European monetary system.
-- Air France in advanced stages of alliance talks with Continental Airlines.
-- UDF conservative party member Francois Leotard calls in interview for lower taxes, notably a cut in VAT and a rethink of government plans to increase petrol duties.
-- One Frenchman in two thinks unemployment will increase in the coming twelve months and remain a problem for the next ten years, survey shows.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- CFDT union leader Nicole Notat and FO leader Marc Blondel to head civil service demonstrations on Thursday.
-- Government to unveil this week which of Alcatel Alsthom or Lagardere is going to win bid for defence electronics group Thomson.
-- Eurocopter aircraft manufacturer hopes to break even by 1997, chairman says.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Honda Motor Europe chairman Kazue Ito says return to profits due to innovative products, intends to tackle central European emerging market.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Naval shipyard workers demonstrated in Paris at weekend against job cuts linked to defence sector restructuring.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Finns give single currency a boost.
-- German Bundesbank's pleas against a loose interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty criteria for European monetary union remain unheeded.
